Lessons.Title: Solve Problems Involving Multiplication
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will solve contextual problems that involve multiplication of a single-digit number and a whole number of up to four digits, or multiplication of 2 two-digit numbers.
This lesson gives you the opportunity to apply the multiplication strategies you have learned to solve various contextual problems involving measurement. The problems vary in format and complexity—some involve a single computation and others require multiple steps to solve. The work here prompts you to make sense of problems and persevere in solving them (MP1) and to reason quantitatively and abstractly (MP2). - Action and Expression
Core relationship: Solve multiplication word problems. Identify equal groups or array factors, multiply and interpret the units.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  What Do You Know About 1 Year?	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Time Flies When We Leap Years	 (25 minutes); Activity 2:  Coin Collection	 (10 minutes); Cool-down:  Leap Year	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: A set has 365 items in each of 4 collections. How many items?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): A class makes 28 packages with 12 stickers each. Total?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Adding factors instead of multiplying repeated groups.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Identify equal groups or array factors, multiply and interpret the units.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using addition where a repeated group count is intended.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The chosen operation or representation does not match the stated context.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Multiply count by the single-group quantity.
